Data Sourcing and Generation Steps:

1. CLONE / SYNC THE ORE ENGINE SOURCE
   Source: OreStudio's fork of the ORE Engine, kept in sync with
   upstream OpenSourceRisk/Engine (this replaces the previous
   "download OreStudio/OreStudio's own zip" instructions below, which
   were stale/incorrect -- that repo is this one, it never contained
   ORE's Examples/xsd; the actual, correct source has always been
   manifest.json's own source_url, OpenSourceRisk/Engine, now tracked
   via OreStudio's own fork so local hand-patches/version pins are
   possible without forking on every refresh).
     git@github.com:OreStudio/Engine.git    (fork, push target)
     git@github.com:OpenSourceRisk/Engine.git   (upstream, pull-only)
   Kept as a separate checkout OUTSIDE this repo (e.g.
   ~/Development/ORE/Engine), not a submodule.
   Commands (first time):
     git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:OreStudio/Engine.git
     cd Engine
     git remote add upstream git@github.com:OpenSourceRisk/Engine.git
   Commands (updating the fork before syncing):
     git fetch upstream
     git checkout master && git merge --ff-only upstream/master
     git submodule update --init --recursive
     git push origin master

2. SYNC EXAMPLES + XSD
   Script: external/ore/tools/update_ore_samples.sh
   Command:
     ./external/ore/tools/update_ore_samples.sh <path-to-ore-engine-checkout>
   Target: external/ore/examples/ (+ its own manifest.json) and
   external/ore/xsd/ (+ its own manifest.json), synced together from the
   same engine commit -- a schema/example version mismatch produces
   spurious validation failures unrelated to either side being wrong.
   Validates every example XML against the freshly synced schema
   automatically (scripts/validate_ore_examples.sh) before finishing.
   See external/ore/examples/methodology.txt and
   external/ore/xsd/README.md for the full detail on what gets
   vendored/excluded.

   KNOWN HAND-PATCHES (reapplied automatically by this script -- do not
   remove without re-verifying against upstream first): 3 files ship a
   genuinely wrong FX/RATE key order from upstream (confirmed against
   QuantLib's own FXSpotQuote convention, not an ORE-Studio-specific
   issue -- see update_ore_samples.sh's own header comment for the
   full explanation and doc/agile/product_backlog/deferred/
   document_ore_vendor_hand_patches.org for the history/PR #1423). If a
   future upstream release fixes this at the source, the script's
   sed patch becomes a no-op (harmless) until explicitly removed once
   confirmed unnecessary.

3. PACKAGE THE ENGINE BINARY
   Script: external/ore/tools/package_ore.sh
   Command:
     ./external/ore/tools/package_ore.sh <path-to-ore-engine-build-dir>
   Target: external/ore/packages/ore-<version>-x64-linux.tar.gz (+
   diff-report.txt + this directory's own manifest.json). See
   external/ore/packages/methodology.txt for the full build/package/
   verify/install detail -- this step needs the engine actually built
   first (cmake --preset + cmake --build against the same checkout
   step 1 produced), not just the source sync from step 2.

4. CODE GENERATION
   Regenerate the codec's record tables from the (freshly synced) XSD
   schemas:
     ./compass.sh generate
   This regenerates the files under:
     - projects/ores.ore/core/include/ores.ore.core/xml/generated
     - projects/ores.ore/core/src/xml/generated
   Run this whenever step 2 changes external/ore/xsd/ content, even if
   examples/ alone changed and packages/ didn't move -- the tables are
   schema-derived, not example-derived.
   The output is a code-shape artefact and the diff is large. Verify it
   with the XML suites, which read and write the whole example corpus,
   not by reading the diff.

5. GENERATE THE SCRIPT LIBRARY DATASET
   Source: external/ore/examples/Products/Input/scriptlibrary.xml, as step 2
   synced it from the engine commit. The other copies of scriptlibrary.xml
   under external/ore/examples/ belong to single examples and are not read.
   Script: external/ore/tools/generate_script_library.py
   Corrections: external/ore/tools/script_library_corrections.json
   Output (in projects/ores.sql/populate/ore/):
     - ore_methodology_populate.sql (this file, as the methodology's text)
     - ore_script_library_dataset_populate.sql (the ore.script_library dataset)
     - ore_script_library_artefact_populate.sql (the staged rows)

   The generator calls the shell's offline script commands, so the shell is
   built first, from the same checkout:
     ./compass.sh build ores.shell
   Commands:
     python3 external/ore/tools/generate_script_library.py
     python3 external/ore/tools/generate_script_library.py --check
   --shell PATH names another build of ores.shell, such as one of another
   preset; the default is
   build/output/linux-clang-release-ninja/publish/bin/ores.shell. --check
   writes nothing and exits non-zero when a committed file differs from what
   the generator makes. No server, database or login is needed.

   The generator derives the staged rows in four steps, in order:
     a. Extraction. Every Script element of the library is read with its
        variants (the purpose attribute, "default" when absent), NPV
        variable, results, calibrations and schedule coarsenings. The
        comment that precedes a script gives its description, its first
        non-blank line, and its inputs' descriptions: the first line of each
        entry under an "Input Data:" or "Inputs:" heading.
     b. Correction. Each entry of script_library_corrections.json names a
        script and variant, the text it replaces, its replacement and the
        reason. A correction applies when its text occurs exactly once, does
        nothing when the code already holds its replacement, and otherwise
        fails the generation, so a library that changes the script is
        reviewed. The file is the only list of corrections.
     c. Parsing. Every variant is parsed by "ores.shell script check", run in
        one batch with --load and an unreachable NATS URL. A script that does
        not parse fails the generation, and the shell's output names its
        line and column.
     d. Derivation of inputs. Every script's inputs are listed by
        "ores.shell script inputs" over its variants, which merges them.

   The populate publishes nothing: the world bundle publishes the staged
   rows into the system tenant at the end of database bring-up, by the
   trading service's publish function, which writes a new version only of a
   script whose rows changed.

   Verification: the generator's --check, run by the build job after the
   shell is built, and ores.trading.scripting.tests, whose inputs test
   derives every staged script's inputs with the parser and compares them.
   Following this step on a fresh checkout reproduces the committed files
   byte for byte. Rerun it after step 2 moves the examples, after a change
   to the corrections, and after a change to the parser that can change a
   script's inputs, which fails --check until the rows are regenerated.

6. COMMIT TO REPOSITORY
   git add external/ore/* projects/ores.ore/core/include/ores.ore.core/xml/generated projects/ores.ore/core/src/xml/generated projects/ores.sql/populate/ore/
   git commit -m "[data] Update ORE Sample Data"
   Commit examples/, xsd/, packages/, and the regenerated domain.hpp/
   domain.cpp together -- they're all derived from the same engine
   commit and should never land out of step with each other.
